title: Prepositions
summary: Prepositions of time and place (in, on, at), preposition collocations that go with particular verbs and adjectives, telling a preposition from a conjunction or an adverb particle, and the fixed pairs the exams test again and again.
learningObjectives: Use in, on and at correctly for time and for place.
Recall the standard preposition that follows common verbs and adjectives.
Distinguish a preposition from a subordinating conjunction and from a phrasal-verb particle.
Fix the fixed-pair errors that recur in error detection (different from, comply with, and so on).

sources.title: English Grammar/Basic Parts of Speech/Prepositions
sources.notes: Used to cross-check the definition and role of prepositions. All collocation lists, example sentences and exercises here are original and reflect current usage.

blocks.title: What a preposition does
blocks.markdown:
A preposition links a noun or pronoun to the rest of the sentence and shows a relation: place, time, direction, cause, manner. The noun after it is its object: *in the drawer*, *after the audit*, *because of the delay*.

Most preposition errors are not about meaning; they are about the fixed word that a particular verb, adjective or noun expects. English fixes these by convention, so they have to be learned as pairs.

blocks.title: In, on, at for time
blocks.markdown:
- **at** for clock times and short points: *at 10 a.m.*, *at noon*, *at midnight*, *at the moment*.
- **on** for days and dates: *on Monday*, *on 3 March*, *on the due date*, *on my birthday*.
- **in** for longer periods: *in June*, *in 2026*, *in the morning*, *in the last quarter*, *in a week's time*.

No preposition before *last*, *next*, *this*, *every*: *last week*, *next month*, *this Friday*, *every day*.
searchKeywords: at 10 am on Monday in June

blocks.title: In, on, at for place
blocks.markdown:
- **at** for a point or a place seen as a point: *at the counter*, *at the entrance*, *at the bus stop*, *at head office*.
- **on** for a surface or a line: *on the shelf*, *on the wall*, *on page 4*, *on the second floor*, *on the coast*.
- **in** for an enclosed space or an area: *in the branch*, *in the drawer*, *in Kolkata*, *in the file*.

Transport takes *on* for large or public vehicles (*on the bus*, *on a train*, *on a flight*) but *in* for cars and taxis (*in the car*).
searchKeywords: at the counter on the shelf in the branch
on the bus in the car

blocks.title: Verbs and adjectives with fixed prepositions
blocks.markdown:
Learn these as units. A sample that recurs in bank exams:

- **comply with**, **abide by**, **adhere to** a rule
- **consist of**, **comprise** (no *of*), **account for** a figure
- **depend on**, **rely on**, **insist on** something
- **refer to**, **respond to**, **subscribe to**, **object to**
- **differ from** / **be different from** (Indian and British English), **similar to**
- **capable of**, **confident of**, **guilty of**, **aware of**
- **eligible for**, **responsible for**, **liable for**, **suitable for**
- **married to**, **superior to**, **prior to**, **senior to** (not *than*)
- **congratulate on**, **accuse of**, **blame for**, **prevent from**

Where a verb already implies the relation, no preposition follows: *discuss the matter* (not *discuss about*), *reach the office* (not *reach to*), *enter the hall* (not *enter into* unless it means "begin", as in *enter into an agreement*).
searchKeywords: comply with depend on different from

blocks.title: Preposition, conjunction or particle?
blocks.markdown:
The same word can appear in more than one class.

- *before* / *after* / *since* / *until*: a **preposition** before a noun (*before the meeting*), a **conjunction** before a clause (*before the meeting started*).
- *up*, *out*, *off*, *on*: a **preposition** when followed by an object showing place (*up the stairs*), a **particle** of a phrasal verb when it is part of the verb's meaning (*fill up the form*, *carry out the audit*).
- *like*: a preposition meaning "similar to" (*a leader like her*); avoid it as a conjunction in formal writing (*as I said*, not *like I said*).

blocks.title: Worked example: choosing the preposition
blocks.markdown:
1. *All staff must comply ____ the revised dress code.* The fixed pair is *comply with*: **with**.

2. *The training will begin ____ 9 a.m. ____ Monday.* A clock time takes *at*; a day takes *on*: **at ... on**.

3. *Her approach is quite different ____ her predecessor's.* Standard Indian and British usage is *different from*: **from**.

4. *The officer was senior ____ everyone else on the panel.* *senior*, *junior*, *superior*, *prior* take *to*, not *than*: **to**.

5. *They will discuss ____ the proposal tomorrow.* *discuss* takes a direct object, so **(no preposition)**.
searchKeywords: comply with senior to different from

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.markdown:
- **discuss about, reach to, enter into (a room), order for.** The verb already carries the relation; drop the preposition.
- **senior/junior/superior/prior than.** These take *to*.
- **different than** in formal Indian and British writing - prefer *different from*.
- **married with** - the correct pair is *married to*.
- **comprise of** - *comprise* takes no *of*; use *consist of* or *be composed of* instead.
- **on / in a newspaper** - an item is *in* a newspaper, but *on* a website or *on* television.
- **since / for** - *since* a point in time, *for* a length of time.

blocks.title: Quick revision
blocks.markdown:
- Time: *at* a clock time, *on* a day or date, *in* a month, year or longer period. No preposition with *last*, *next*, *this*, *every*.
- Place: *at* a point, *on* a surface or line, *in* an enclosed space or area.
- Collocations are fixed: *comply with*, *depend on*, *different from*, *capable of*, *eligible for*, *senior to*.
- Verbs that already imply the relation take a direct object: *discuss*, *reach*, *enter (a place)*, *request*, *order*.
- Before a clause use the conjunction form (*before it started*); before a noun use the preposition (*before the start*).

blocks.title: Practice
blocks.markdown:
Choose the correct preposition; give a one-line reason.

1. The meeting is ___ 3 p.m.
2. Your appraisal is due ___ March.
3. She has worked here ___ five years.
4. The file is ___ the drawer.
5. Put your signature ___ the dotted line.
6. He is responsible ___ the cash counter.
7. This draft is different ___ the earlier one.
8. They travelled ___ Delhi to Mumbai by train.

flashcards.front: at / on / in for: 9 a.m., Monday, June?
flashcards.back: at 9 a.m. (clock time), on Monday (day), in June (month). Longer period takes 'in'.
flashcards.explanation: Point in time = at; day/date = on; month/year/part-of-day = in.

flashcards.front: Which preposition before "last week", "next month", "every day"?
flashcards.back: None. "last", "next", "this" and "every" take no preposition before a time word.
flashcards.explanation: "on last Monday" is wrong; just "last Monday".

flashcards.front: Complete: "All staff must comply ____ the code."
flashcards.back: "with". Also: abide by, adhere to, conform to.
"different from" in standard Indian and British usage. "similar to", but "different from".
flashcards.explanation: "different than" is avoided in formal writing here.

flashcards.front: senior, junior, superior, prior — which preposition, never 'than'?
flashcards.back: "to": senior to, junior to, superior to, prior to.
flashcards.explanation: These Latin comparatives already carry the comparison.

flashcards.back: No. "discuss" takes a direct object: "discuss the proposal". Same with reach, enter (a place), request, order.
flashcards.explanation: The verb already contains the relation.

flashcards.front: "before" the meeting vs "before" the meeting started — same word, what changes?
flashcards.back: Before a noun (the meeting) it is a preposition; before a clause (the meeting started) it is a conjunction.
